correctness.rationale: For arbitrary p,q, supporting-line slopes at the endpoints of the perpendicular-bisector chord are bounded by the chord half-length, while the angle between the corresponding triangle sides is at least the minimum interior angle; convexity of tan gives the universal lower bound. The minimum-angle bisector attains equality. Splitting triangles by whether the smallest enclosing disk is diameter- or circumcircle-controlled yields explicit half-angle formulas whose one-variable monotonicity gives the sharp fatness envelopes.

originality.rationale: Pach--Tardos introduced the invariant and proved only general comparison bounds plus disk and square examples. Targeted web and archive searches found no evaluation for arbitrary triangles, no half-minimum-angle formula, and no sharp triangle-specific conversion window to inradius/smallest-enclosing-disk fatness.

value.rationale: The result exactly identifies a new convex-body roundness invariant with the classical minimum-angle quality parameter on triangles, determines the full sharp fatness range at fixed roundness, and improves the general lower conversion constant 0.28 to the optimal triangle constant sqrt(3)/2.
